Final preregistration for the small WASM occupancy experiment: the actual default preflight has now passed under root review (command below, exit 0). All 312 planted cipher configurations recover exactly 546 bytes from the synthetic alphabet 0x80..0xA7, and the full/tail detector controls pass. No Rev7 decryption has run in this experiment yet.

Frozen target scope: 5 orientations (forward, complete hex-character reverse, byte-pair reverse, within-byte nibble swap, and true visible-token reversal with widths [2]+[5]*218). Each has 19 block primitives x 4 modes (cfb8/ncfb/ofb/ctr) x 2 literal keys (Zombies/ZOMBIES) x 2 IVs (zero/ASCII0), plus 4 stream primitives x 2 keys. This is 1,560 decryptions and 3,080 windows: full outputs and one-native-block-skipped tails for block primitives, full outputs only for streams. The key buffer is cleared before every call; Loki97 explicitly uses a 32-byte zero-padded key. This is a stable specified implementation, not a model of arbitrary historical stale heap bytes.

Scoring is the published exact length-aware distinct-byte threshold at 9a80dd1e, per-output iid-uniform tail at most 1e-15. A flag means retain and inspect, not plaintext. Short or out-of-range windows are untested. Every descriptor, output length and hash, and full/tail score is retained; every flagged output additionally retains exact bytes. Errors remain explicit. No additional keys, adaptive orientations, or arbitrary-IV claims.
